subject: Flowly POC — liquidity credits vs. short extension
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@flowly.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on POC runway — can we add 3 weeks?

Hey Markus,

Thanks again for the support during the POC — the infra team has been able to ramp our ingestion tests and we want to run an additional set of latency experiments against full user traces. We're about 70% through the validation plan but need another 3 weeks to finish the remaining scenarios.

Two procurement options on our side:
- We can buy a short 3-week addendum (invoice up front).
- Or we can take a smaller, discounted credit bucket to cover the extra usage (apply against the hosted tokens).

Can Redwood provide a pricing option for both? Our finance person (procurement@flowly.ai) needs a ballpark today so we can decide quickly. Also let me know if there are any constraints on preserving the same model/throughput during the extension.

Appreciate it —
Lydia
Lydia Park
Head of ML Platforms, Flowly
lydia.park@flowly.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@flowly.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on POC runway — can we add 3 weeks?

Hi Lydia,

Appreciate the heads-up — glad the tests are moving forward. I sketched two concrete options below so procurement can choose what fits Flowly's approval path. Attaching a short amendment and a pricing matrix for reference.

Option A — Short-term addendum (standard invoice)
- 3 weeks of the same capacity as your current pool
- Fixed fee: $18,000 (covers peak concurrency + engineering support during the window)
- Invoiced net 30; can be a separate PO line item

Option B — Liquidity credits (applied to hosted tokens)
- Purchase a credit bucket equivalent to expected token burn for 3 weeks
- One-time purchase with 20% volume discount off published pay-as-you-go rates
- Credits redeemable against the current Flowly account, valid for 90 days

Notes/constraints:
- If you need guaranteed identical throughput, choose Option A (reserved concurrency for the window). Option B is lower friction but subject to capacity policies; we'll prioritize but not reserve GPU pools.
- If you commit to a post-POC quarterly usage commitment within 30 days of conversion, we can increase the credit discount to 25%.

Next steps:
- If procurement prefers Option A, send PO to finance@redwood.com and we'll attach the addendum.
- If Option B, let me know bucket size and I'll generate the credit invoice.

I've attached: Flowly-POC-Amendment-v1.pdf (legal summary) and flowly-extension-pricing-matrix.xlsx (line items). Looping in David in case you want engineering bandwidth guarantees.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
From: procurement@flowly.ai
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia.park@flowly.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on POC runway — can we add 3 weeks?

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the options. Procurement's preference is Option B (credits) because it's faster on our PO process. A couple clarifying questions before we raise a PO:
1) How exactly are credits consumed — token-first or spike-first? We need an audit trail for usage.
2) If capacity throttling occurs under Option B, will Redwood commit to a minimum SLA for the 3-week window or offer credits back?
3) We need the invoice and SOW language to reference the Flowly PO# F-2026-1146.

If you can confirm the answers and send an invoice (net 30) with the discounted line applied, we can get the PO signed today.

Regards,
Flowly Procurement
procurement@flowly.ai

> Thanks for the options. Procurement's preference is Option B (credits) because it's faster on our PO process. A couple clarifying questions before we raise a PO:
> 1) How exactly are credits consumed — token-first or spike-first? We need an audit trail for usage.
> 2) If capacity throttling occurs under Option B, will Redwood commit to a minimum SLA for the 3-week window or offer credits back?

Hi — quick answers inline and next steps. Looping Kimberly (finance) to confirm invoice flow and David (solutions) for capacity/SLA nuance.

Answers:
1) Credits are deducted token-first against your account usage; they'll show up in the billing exports and the Console's token ledger. We can provide a daily consumption CSV for the duration for your audit team.
2) Option B is not a capacity reservation. We will prioritize your requests and can offer an operational credit (pro-rated) if capacity constraints caused higher-than-expected latency and we fail to meet the agreed performance band. For full guaranteed throughput we recommend Option A.
3) Kimberly will issue the invoice and include the PO reference. Kimberly — can you confirm net 30 invoice and apply the 20% discount line item?

David: for the SLA carve, do you want me to propose the language that says "operational credit up to X% if requests exceed latency thresholds for more than Y% of the window"?

Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>:
> We can issue an invoice with PO# and net 30. I can apply the 20% discount for this credit bucket. If Flowly elects to convert to a quarterly commitment within 30 days, finance will process a 5% retrospective rebate.

David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>:
> I will draft suggested SLA credit language and forward a short ops-runbook for the 3-week window (monitoring hooks, escalation path).

If that works, Lydia/procurement — reply with the intended credit bucket size (tokens estimate) and I'll generate the invoice + drive link to the amendment for signature.

Thanks —
